verdict.rationale: Babylon.js clearly ships a credible WebGPU story alongside WebGL 1.0/2.0 (docs-10, docs-22, docs-27, docs-39) and offers tree-shakable ES6/NPM modules aimed at reducing payload (docs-24, docs-25). However, hands-on community reports concretely contradict the 'reasonable payload' half of the story: one developer notes Babylon is 'three times the size of ThreeJS, so bandwidth optimization is required' (babylonjs-comm-5), and another reports a demo scene took ~5 minutes to download 50MB, questioning whether download times become a limiting factor (babylonjs-comm-17). missing for 10: independent bundle-size benchmarks after tree-shaking, first-party guidance/case studies showing typical production payload sizes, and resolution of the size-vs-ThreeJS complaint.
